slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only populated slot observed in the single sample; EEPROM sector index = slot_number * 0x1b (27 sectors * 8 bytes/sector = 216 bytes/slot), derived from FUN_08016198/FUN_080160b4 computing `sector_base = (param_1 & 0xff) * 0x1b`.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_1 (hypothesis)
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: HYPOTHESIS ONLY: not proven by code or data. Entirely 0xFF in the single available sample (bytes 0xD8-0xC7+0xD8 range unobserved as non-blank). Inferred purely from the 0x1b-sector slot stride supporting a second slot_number value; no second-slot write/read call site was found in the 321 traced functions.

slots_and_copies.name: tail_region (hypothesis)
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: HYPOTHESIS ONLY: remaining 80 bytes (512 - 2*216) of the 512-byte EEPROM are unaccounted for by the 0x1b-sector slot stride; entirely 0xFF in the sample. No code path in the trace references this region directly.

checksums.name: slot_payload_byte_sum16
checksums.formula_detail: Unsigned byte-wise sum (no rollover masking beyond 16 bits) of the 200-byte slot payload (offsets 0x00-0xC7 inclusive, which itself ends with the 4-byte 'CARS' magic trailer at 0xC4-0xC7). Proven in FUN_08016198 (RAM-cached validation branch): `do { iStack_20 += buf[uVar8]; uVar8++; } while (uVar8 < 200);` followed by a comparison against a cached RAM checksum variable (`*piRam080162ac`). The EEPROM-resident write path in the same function (via FUN_0802ad98, a confirmed EEPROM-write helper) targets sector `slot*0x1b + 0x1a` (byte offset 0xD0-0xD1 for slot 0), which does NOT match the offset of the numeric match found in the sample (0xD6-0xD7). The algorithm itself is CONFIRMED_STATIC; the exact persisted storage offset is only a verified numeric coincidence pending more samples.

io_driver_functions.notes: Shared low-level DMA3 serial bit-transceiver over the EEPROM bus (0x0D000000, gated via REG_DMA3CNT 0x040000D4-equivalent access through _DAT_08037978/_DAT_0803798c pointers). Direction (TX vs RX) is determined entirely by caller-supplied bit-count and buffer args; it is the common primitive for both read and write framing, not a save-specific writer/reader by itself.

EEPROM low-level sector READ: encodes a 'read' command + sector address bitstream, issues it via FUN_08037918 (TX), then issues a second FUN_08037918 call requesting 0x44=68 bits back (4 dummy/lead bits + 64 data bits), decodes 4x16-bit words MSB-first into the destination buffer (param_2). One sector = 8 bytes (4 u16 words).

EEPROM low-level sector WRITE: encodes a 'write' command + sector address + 64 data bits read from the source buffer (param_2), transmits via a single FUN_08037918 TX call, then busy-waits on what is almost certainly REG_VCOUNT (pointer _DAT_08037b48) for ~0x88 (136) scanline deltas to let the EEPROM commit the write internally (standard ~10ms EEPROM write-busy behavior). param_3 selects retry-forever vs single-attempt wait.
Thin wrapper: `FUN_08037a5c(param_1, param_2, 1)` — forces the forever-retry wait variant of the low-level EEPROM write.

Write-verification helper: re-reads the just-written sector via FUN_08037998 into a local 8-byte buffer and compares it word-by-word against the caller-supplied buffer, returning 0 on match or 0x8000 on mismatch. Used after every sector write to confirm the EEPROM actually committed the data.

Mid-level EepromWrite(sector, src_buf, byte_count): writes full 8-byte-aligned chunks directly via FUN_08037a48+FUN_08037bbc; for a trailing partial sector it performs read-modify-write (reads the existing sector via FUN_08037998, overwrites only the first N remaining bytes, writes the merged sector back via FUN_08037a48+FUN_08037bbc) so unrelated bytes already in that sector are preserved.

Mid-level EepromRead(sector, dest_buf, byte_count): mirror of FUN_0802ad98 for reads — full 8-byte-aligned chunks read directly via FUN_08037998+FUN_08037bbc verify, trailing partial sector read into a temp buffer and the needed leading bytes copied out to dest_buf.

Slot WRITE/validate entry point. If a RAM-resident cached copy of the slot is already marked valid (`*(int*)(cache_base+0xc0) == marker`), it recomputes the 200-byte checksum from the RAM buffer and validates it plus a structured sanity scan (byte fields < thresholds across 16 x 12-byte records at RAM+5) against a cached expected checksum (`*piRam080162ac`) — no EEPROM I/O in this path. Otherwise it builds/refreshes the slot payload in RAM and writes it (200 bytes via FUN_0802ad98) plus a 2-byte trailer (also via FUN_0802ad98, sector `slot*0x1b+0x1a`) to EEPROM, returning a status code (0/1/2/3/4) depending on which branch and whether the writes verified.

Slot LOAD entry point: reads 200 bytes + a 2-byte trailer from EEPROM via FUN_0802ae48 for slot `param_1`. If either read/verify fails, it falls back to calling FUN_08016198(param_1) to (re)write a fresh/default slot image, i.e. acts as the load-with-repair-on-corruption path. No caller of FUN_080160b4 exists inside the 321 traced functions — it is the top of the traced save call chain.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Unknown — no caller of 0x080160b4 is present in the 321-function trace, so the gameplay/menu event that invokes a slot load was not captured.

fields.name: unlock_flag_block
fields.ram_addr: 0x02000000-ish (cache buffer, exact EWRAM address not resolved from this trace subset)

observed_values.as_u32_le_array: 37 little-endian u32 values, each exactly 0 or 1

fields.update_mechanism: Populated in RAM before the 200-byte EepromWrite call inside FUN_08016198; exact per-flag writer logic lies outside the 321 traced functions.
fields.evidence: Every 4-byte little-endian dword from offset 0x00 to 0x93 in saves/cap-00-future-0.sav is exactly 0 or 1 (verified by direct Python struct-unpack over all 37 dwords); layout matches the 200-byte region covered by the checksum in FUN_08016198.

fields.name: structured_record_block
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; no writer logic for individual sub-fields observed inside the 321 traced functions — only the whole-buffer EEPROM write/read is traced.
fields.evidence: Byte pattern (small values in bytes 0-2, zero/near-zero in byte 3, with paired duplicate dwords at 0x94/0x98 vs 0xa4/0xa8 vs 0xac/0xb0) is suggestive of small counters, times, or per-category best-record pairs, but no code, checksum boundary, or second sample confirms semantics. No third-party labels were consulted per clean-room rules.

fields.name: slot_magic
fields.update_mechanism: Falls inside the 200-byte checksummed payload; written as part of the same FUN_0802ad98(sector,buf,200) call. The specific instruction that stores the literal 0x43415253/'CARS' bytes into the RAM buffer was not found among the 321 traced functions (no immediate-load of that constant appears in ghidra/decompiled.c).
fields.evidence: Bytes 0xC4-0xC7 of saves/cap-00-future-0.sav are exactly '43 41 52 53' = ASCII 'CARS'; this falls within the 200-byte range (0x00-0xC7) proven to be the checksum coverage window in FUN_08016198.

fields.name: payload_checksum
writers: 0x08016198 (algorithm); exact storage-offset writer unresolved, see checksums[] entry
fields.update_mechanism: Computed as the unsigned byte-sum of offsets 0x00-0xC7 (200 bytes); recomputed and compared on every validate-from-RAM-cache pass in FUN_08016198.
fields.evidence: Python verification: sum(data[0x00:0xc8]) & 0xffff == 0x150, and int.from_bytes(data[0xd6:0xd8],'big') == 0x150 — an exact match, but the EEPROM-write call site for this checksum in the traced code (FUN_0802ad98 at sector slot*0x1b+0x1a) addresses byte offset 0xD0-0xD1, not 0xD6-0xD7, so the storage-offset mapping is not fully reconciled against the algorithm's own call-site arithmetic from a single sample.

fields.name: unused_tail_padding
fields.update_mechanism: Unwritten/blank fill; part of the trailing EEPROM sectors 25-26 not touched by the 200-byte primary write.
fields.evidence: Offsets 0xC8-0xD5 are uniformly 0xFF in the sole available sample (background fill byte per packet metadata).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt the 'CARS' magic (e.g. flip to 'XARS') and reload via a paired pre/post .ss state at the title/load-slot screen.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the magic is part of the checksummed 200-byte region as mapped, corrupting it changes the computed sum, so the HYPOTHESIS checksum at 0xD6-0xD7 would also need recomputation to avoid a validation failure; predicted observable effect is the game treating the slot as invalid/corrupt and falling back to FUN_08016198's default-write/repair path (visible as a reset save or 'new game' prompt).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip the candidate checksum bytes at 0xD6-0xD7 without touching the payload.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this is truly the checksum location, the game should detect mismatch and trigger the repair/reset path on load; if nothing observably changes, this falsifies the HYPOTHESIS storage offset and supports the alternative 0xD0-0xD1 location implied by the traced write call-site.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip individual boolean dwords in the 0x00-0x93 flag block one at a time (0<->1).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Each flip should toggle one discrete in-game unlock/progress boolean (car, track, or mode unlock) if the checksum is also repaired to the new sum; if checksum repair uses the 0xD6-0xD7 offset and the game still accepts the save, this corroborates the HYPOTHESIS location.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero out the structured_record_block (offsets 0x94-0xC3) with checksum repair.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If these are best-time/score records, zeroing should reset displayed records to a default/blank state rather than crashing; a crash or garbage display would indicate these bytes encode something more structurally sensitive (e.g. pointers or indices) than flat counters.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Write non-0xFF bytes into the hypothesized tail_region (offsets 0x1B0-0x1FF) with no other changes.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this region is genuinely unused by the traced code, no behavior change is expected on load; any observable change (crash, corrupted UI, different slot behavior) would indicate an untraced consumer of this region exists.

open_questions: What function actually constructs the in-RAM 200-byte payload (including writing the literal 'CARS' magic bytes) before FUN_08016198 calls FUN_0802ad98? It is not among the 321 functions in ghidra/decompiled.c.

Why does the single available sample's apparent checksum value (sum16 of bytes 0x00-0xC7 = 0x150) numerically match bytes at offset 0xD6-0xD7, when the traced EEPROM-write call site for the 2-byte trailer addresses sector slot*0x1b+0x1a = byte offset 0xD0-0xD1 (which is blank/0xFF in the sample)? Needs a second non-blank sample or a direct write-time memory trace to resolve.

Is there really a second save slot (bytes 216-431) and/or a distinct global-config tail region (bytes 432-511), or does the whole 512-byte EEPROM belong to a single slot with a different internal layout than the 0x1b-sector stride suggests? No second-slot call site (param_1 != 0) was found in the trace.

What do the 12 structured bytes at 0x94-0xC3 represent? No semantics can be assigned without either additional samples showing variation, paired .ss RAM state at the moment of writing, or an authorized gameplay probe.

What is the exact RAM/EWRAM address of the slot cache buffer (_DAT_08016230/_DAT_08016144) and the cache-valid marker compared at cache_base+0xc0 vs _DAT_08016234? Not resolvable from static decompilation alone; would require a live emulator RAM-watch trace.

Is FUN_08037918's wait/poll register at _DAT_08037b48 actually REG_VCOUNT (0x04000006)? Plausible given the ~136-scanline busy-wait threshold matching known EEPROM write-commit timing, but not proven since no MMIO base-address constants are visible in this decompiled subset.
